Subject: Deployment rollback and operator handover — clarifications

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward the Order Form signature, our legal and ops teams asked for clarification on two private-deployment items that need to be reflected in the MSA addendum:

1) Rollback / exit mechanics — we need a clear, contract-backed runbook that describes how Acme can rollback to our previous on-prem model if we decide to decommission the Redwood service. Specifically: what artifacts, configs, and container images (if any) will Redwood deliver — and under which conditions.

2) Secure handover — we cannot accept operator-level access from third parties. We need an auditable handover package (runbook, TLS certs export instructions, scripts, and a manifest) and an attestation that no source code or proprietary model weights will be transferred.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will: (a) deliver a runbook and signed attestation only, (b) provide a snapshot of runtime artifacts under escrow, or (c) offer a buildable artifact bundle including images? Also, what evidence can you provide for audits (signed receipt, transfer logs, or notarized escrow)?

We're on a tight procurement timeline — would like to have the addendum language finalized by the end of next week.

Best,
Sanjay
Procurement Manager, Acme Health

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: Redwood is happy to include a firmed-up runbook and a signed attestation in the addendum. We have three practical delivery options and can mark which one is contractually binding:

A) Handover package (preferred for most customers): runbook + operational manifests + scripts + signed attestation that no source code or model weights are transferred. No operator credentials will be handed over.
B) Escrow snapshot (limited): encrypted snapshot of specific runtime artifacts (container images and manifests) deposited with a neutral escrow agent; release conditions are specified in the addendum (e.g., breach, insolvency, sustained SLA failure). Agent fees and retrieval process are extra.
C) Buildable artifact bundle (only by exception): a set of artifacts sufficient to rebuild runtime; this is heavy and typically requires additional licensing and review.

I'll loop in our legal and ops folks to propose tight addendum language and the audit evidence we can provide (signed attestation, transfer logs, retrieval receipts, and notarized escrow options).

I'll follow up internally and send suggested redlines by EOD.

Mina / Laura — quick ops take:

- Option A: fully doable. We can produce a runbook that includes rollback steps, manifest verification commands, artifact manifests (hashes), and a canonical checklist for handover. Delivery timeline: 7 business days from signed addendum (assuming we don't need to generate images). Evidence: signed attestation + export log + artifact hash list.
- Option B: escrow snapshot is feasible but has lead time. We need to specify an approved escrow provider (we typically use Custodia Partners), encryption key custody model, and a retrieval / release flow requiring dual-signer approval (Redwood + customer) or tribunal trigger. Lead time: 3-4 weeks to create and deposit snapshot; escrow costs borne by customer.
- Option C: buildable bundle — this is work-intensive and requires a special licensing appendix. Not recommended unless Acme has a compelling regulatory need.

Operational guardrails to include in redlines (suggested):
- Scope-limited artifacts only: runtime manifests and supporting scripts; no model weights, no training data, no internal toolchain code.
- Release triggers: insolvency, material breach, or agreed SLA failure window (X days beyond SLO).
- Escrow retrieval process: notarized request + 10-business-day notice + verification period.

I'll assemble an ops checklist and sample runbook excerpt and attach to the redlines doc.

—Marcus

Sanjay —

Thanks for the patience. We've reviewed internally and attached a proposed redline (MSA_Addendum_ACME_v2_redlines.docx) and a short handover/runbook outline (handover_runbook_outline.pdf). Summary of our position:

- Default commitment (included in the addendum): Redwood will deliver a handover package (Option A) upon valid termination or customer-requested decommission. The package will include: a detailed runbook, operational manifests with artifact hashes, automation scripts to assist verification, and a signed attestation that no Redwood proprietary source code or model weights are being transferred. No operator credentials will be provided.
- Escrow snapshot (Option B) is available as a paid, optional add-on. Escrow requires a named escrow agent, encrypted deposit, and a clearly defined release trigger (insolvency / material breach / sustained SLA failure). Costs for escrow setup and custody will be borne by Acme.
- Buildable artifact bundle (Option C) is only available under a separate commercial and licensing appendix and is not part of standard delivery.

Audit evidence we can provide: signed attestation, artifact export logs with hashes & timestamps, and escrow deposit receipts if Option B chosen. We have included proposed redline text for each of the above.

Requesting two quick confirmations from Acme to finalize:
1) Which option (A/B/C) do you want to lock in the addendum as default?
2) If B or C, will Acme accept escrow costs & a 3–4 week lead time for snapshot deposit?

If you confirm Option A, we can accept the addendum with our proposed wording and target execution by next Friday.
